versions.localizedDescription:
### Changed
- **The scanner waits longer before committing a card it is unsure of.** Auto-capture fires after two steady frames when the set code *and* collector number confirm the exact printing, but a scan that had only recognised the card's name was being committed after three — and a name-only match takes whichever printing Scryfall's fuzzy search hands back, which is very often not the card on the table. Name-only now needs six steady frames and set-only three, which is what the code had documented all along
- **The scanner's blur check costs a sixteenth of what it did.** Deciding whether a frame is sharp enough to read ran a Laplacian across every pixel of every frame, on the same thread that draws the camera preview — about 5 ms a frame at 1080p, for a number that only gates the OCR. It now takes the same measurement over a stepped, staggered grid of points: the same estimate, far fewer samples
- **The scanner stops asking Scryfall the same unanswerable question.** A lookup that fails is now remembered for ten seconds. Failures are still not cached for the session — OCR noise must not block a name — but with no memory at all the frame loop re-issued up to three requests *per frame* for as long as the camera sat on a card it could not resolve, which is exactly when you hold still and wait
- **A stalled network no longer freezes the scanner for fifteen seconds.** Nothing else is processed while a frame is in flight, so the lookup timeout was also how long the camera outline, the OCR and the readout stopped moving — indistinguishable from a crash. A scan frame gives up after three seconds and the next one tries again; the printing picker, which you are actually waiting on, keeps the full fifteen

- **The scanner converts a third of the pixels it used to, per frame.** Checking whether a frame is sharp only ever looks at a sixteenth of it, but the whole frame was being converted to grayscale first to make that check possible. It now reads the frame where it lies and converts only what the card-outline detector needs, which is a smaller picture than the camera sends. On iPhone at 1080p a frame costs 4.7 ms of that work instead of 1.6, and a frame that turns out to be blurry — the common case while you are still moving the camera — costs 1.0 ms instead of 4.5

### Fixed
- **A printing detail that *disagreed* counted the same as one that was never read.** If the set code came off the card clearly and the match came back from a different set, the confidence figure said what it says when there is no set code at all — "nothing is known" — when what was actually known was a conflict. Each contradicted detail now costs the score, weighted by how far that reading can be trusted: the set code most, the printed year least, since reprints carry a range of years
- **The scanner read the card's name from the wrong line.** Among the text at the top of the card it picked the *longest* line, but the name is the *largest* one — so the type line and the first line of rules text were routinely chosen over the title. Size decides now, and length only settles ties between lines of the same size, such as the two halves of a long title
- **Card names with accented letters were looked up with the accents deleted**, not replaced: "Jötun Grunt" went to Scryfall as "Jtun Grunt" and "Æther Vial" as "ther Vial"
- **The scanner's name and printing windows shifted with the quality setting.** The band the name is read from was a fixed pixel height, which is a third of the frame at 480p and a seventh at 1080p; both windows are now a fraction of the frame
- **On Android the printing strip covered more than half the card instead of the bottom fifth**, because it was measured against the camera buffer's height while the text was being read out of a frame that had been rotated a quarter turn. Rules text and power/toughness in the middle of the card could be mistaken for a collector number or a set code
- **The scanner's requests to Scryfall went out in bursts.** A lookup that falls back from an exact printing to a name search makes up to three requests, and only the first was spaced — the rest left together, against a service that asks for a tenth of a second between them
- **The scanner kept the last card it recognised on screen after the name stopped being readable.** Every other way a frame can fail clears the readout; the one where OCR returns a name too garbled to look up just gave up quietly, leaving the previous card's name and its confidence bar under a camera that was by then pointed at something else

### Changed
- **The collection is now read-only on the phone, all the way.** 0.13.0 took the +/− stepper and the edit and delete buttons off each row but left the same actions behind a long press, which was still collection management on a device that does not manage collections. The long press is gone too: a card opens its detail and nothing else. Cards still reach a binder the moment a scan session is saved — which is when you actually know where they belong — and binders are still created, renamed and deleted from the binder row

### Added
- **The card detail sheet now matches the website's.** Tapping a card still opens instantly on what the phone already has — image, mana cost, type, rules text, your quantity and condition — and then fills in what only the server knows: format legality, the set's full name and rarity, prices in **both** currencies at once, and a price-history chart over 7 days to a year. Double-faced cards get a flip button. None of it needs an account: card data is public, so this works signed out, and the sheet still opens and stays useful with no signal at all
- **You can finally scan another player's QR code into a seat.** Everything behind it already existed — the scanner sheet, the seat link, and the whole path into the uploaded match — but nothing ever opened it, so the code on your Player Card was a code nobody could read. Each seat on the setup screen now carries a scan button; scanning marks the seat as verified, and tapping it again clears the link if you scanned the wrong person. Phones only, since it needs a camera
- **Post-game stats now show where each player sat in the turn order** — who went first, second and so on, as "2 / 4". The app has recorded this all along and already sent it to the website; the phone simply never read it back
- **History marks games from your account the same way the collection does** — the "Web" badge, instead of an icon whose tooltip a phone has no way to show. Games waiting on your answer keep their own mark

### Changed
- **The app is portrait now, except at the table.** Player setup and the live game still turn sideways — they draw a table you sit around — and everything else stands upright: the home screen, History, post-game stats, the collection, Settings, the scanner, the login form and the profile and deck editors. It used to be the other way round, with landscape everywhere and four screens opting out one at a time
- **The home screen shows two tiles per row in portrait** instead of squeezing three across
- **The collection no longer offers buttons that manage nothing.** Cards get into the collection by scanning or from your account, so each row's +/− stepper and its edit and delete buttons are gone; the count is still shown, and a long press still opens the actions. Foil printings are marked with a ✨ in front of the card name instead of a chip after it, and "Normal" — which was never worth saying — is gone from both the list and the card sheet

### Fixed
- **The poison counter's icon sat visibly high in its circle** — 7.7 points of space above it against 10.2 below. Flutter draws icons as text, and Material's glyphs sit about an eighth of their size above the middle of the box the font gives them, which is invisible in a row of icons and obvious inside a small circle
- **The Settings options ran off the right edge of a phone screen.** The font row lost an option behind the overflow marker, and scanner quality clipped too. The option buttons now wrap onto a second line instead of being cut off
- **Prices ignored the currency you chose in Settings.** Which currency a card was priced in was decided by the card's *language* — German printings in euros, everything else in dollars — so a EUR user read dollar figures under a € sign on every English card in their collection, and in the scanner. Prices now follow the setting everywhere: the collection list and card sheet, the scanner's results and printing picker, price sorting, and the CSV export's effective price. A card with no figure in your currency shows the other one with *its* own symbol, rather than mislabelling it
- **Removing a player from the setup screen could hand their seat's scanned player card to somebody else.** The seat-linked data was keyed by seat number and did not move when the seats below it shifted up, so a finished game could have been attributed to the wrong person's account. Never reachable before now, since nothing could scan a card in
- **The scanner's session total was two half-totals.** It showed a dollar sum of the non-German cards stacked above a euro sum of the German ones, so neither number was the value of the pile in front of you. It is now one total, in your currency

### Removed
- **The Light and Dark themes are gone.** Only Colorful was ever finished — the tile palette, the game board and the player tiles are all designed against a black ground, and the other two sat in Settings as struck-through buttons you could not select. The theme picker has been removed with them
- **The Inter and Roboto fonts are gone** from the font picker. OpenSans, Lato, Nunito and Poppins remain
- **The scanner's "Max" quality setting is gone.** It asked the camera for the largest frame the sensor can produce — far more pixels than card recognition needs, and enough work per frame to make the preview stutter. 1080p is the ceiling now; anyone on Max moves to 720p

### Added
- **Confirm games other players logged you into, on the phone** — when someone else records a game and names you in it, that game now appears at the top of History under *Games to confirm*, with the date, the winner and everyone at the table. **That was me** adds it to your history and statistics; **Not me** removes the invitation and leaves the other player's own record untouched. Until now this could only be answered on the website, even though the phone is where the game was played
- History no longer shows "no games yet" when the only thing you have is account content — a fresh install with games shared by other players now shows them
- **The History tile carries a badge** when games are waiting on your answer, so you do not have to open the screen to find out. It refreshes on sign-in and whenever the app comes back to the foreground, and counts down as you answer

### Added
- **The Collection colour filter now asks a real question** — pick how the selected colours should be read: *Exactly these* (only cards of precisely those colours), *At most these* (everything that fits in a deck of those colours, colourless included), *Including these* (cards using at least those colours), or *Commander colors* (what's legal in a Commander deck of those colours, judged on colour identity). Previously the only behaviour was "including", with no way to say otherwise
- **Filter by colour identity instead of mana cost** — a checkbox next to the mode. Colour identity counts mana symbols in a card's rules text, which is what Commander legality is judged on, so a colourless-costed card like Golos reads as five colours rather than none. Implied, and locked on, in Commander mode
- **Filter by how many colours a card has** — a 0–5 range slider, independent of which colours are picked, so "any two-colour card" or "colourless only" is one drag
- Cards now store the colours and colour identity Scryfall reports. Cards scanned or synced before this fall back to reading their mana cost, which cannot see a land's identity — rescanning or refreshing fills it in properly

### Fixed
- **0.12.1 could not be built for iOS** and never reached anyone; everything listed under it below ships here instead

### Added
- **Games logged by other players now appear in your History** — when someone you played with uploads a match and names you in it, and you've confirmed it on the website, it shows up on your phone too, marked as coming from your account. Games this device recorded are never listed twice. Pull down to refresh
- **History shows which games have reached your account** — a cloud icon on each game says whether it's been published or is still waiting. Only appears when match upload is switched on, since it's off by default
- **Scanned cards can be published straight to your ManaVortex-Web account** — when signed in, "Save to Collection" sends the whole session to your account instead of saving it on the device, and can file it into one of your binders or a new one you name on the spot. Cards the server can't match stay in the session rather than being silently dropped. Signed out, everything works exactly as before and stays local
- **Tapping a card in Collection opens a detail view** — full image, mana cost, type line, card text, set, printing, condition, finish and price. Tapping a card previously did nothing at all; everything was hidden behind a long-press nobody would find. Reads entirely from data already on the device, so it works offline
- **Collection filtering and sorting** — filter by name, colour, condition and foil, and sort by name, newest, price or quantity, from a new button in the Collection toolbar. Binder chips stay as the fast path along the top
- **Each deck now shows its win/loss record** when picking a deck for a seat, right-aligned beside the name, with the deck name and commander centred against the commander art
- **Mana costs now render as real symbols instead of raw text** — scanned and collection cards showed `{2}{U}{U}` literally; they now use the same Scryfall Manamoji artwork the website uses, bundled in the app so it works offline. Same 90 images and the same basename rule as the web, so a symbol looks identical on both

### Changed
- **Deck import by URL now supports Archidekt** as well as Moxfield, and both import dialogs are finally translated instead of being English-only
- **Moxfield import now explains itself instead of just failing** — Moxfield blocks other apps from reading decks, so both the username and URL paths now say so and point you at exporting the deck and uploading it on the website, or using Archidekt. Detected when it happens rather than assumed, so it starts working again by itself if Moxfield ever opens back up
- **Poison and commander tax swapped how they're shown** — commander tax now has the always-visible −/+ counter poison used to have, since casting your commander comes up most games; poison collapses to just its icon until you tap it, since usually it never comes up at all. Tapping anywhere on the tax chip still casts, as before — the −/+ are additions, not a replacement. Taking back a mis-tapped cast is now a real button instead of an undiscoverable long-press (which, it turns out, did nothing at all)
- **"Scan Cards" is no longer on the Collection screen** — scanning is a top-level destination on the home screen, and the floating button here covered the last row of cards

### Fixed
- **Buttons had no visible hover state on desktop** — the theme never set `hoverColor`/`splashColor`, so every hover used Flutter's ~4% default, which is invisible over the app's saturated tiles. Several buttons also wrapped an opaque `Container` inside their `InkWell`, which hides the ripple entirely (Material paints ink *beneath* its children); those now use `Ink` so the highlight covers the whole button
- **Horizontal lists couldn't be dragged with a mouse** — most visibly the Collection binder strip, which was unreachable past the first few binders on desktop. Flutter's default scroll behaviour excludes the mouse from drag devices; the app now opts it back in everywhere
- **"Delete all profiles and decks" removed your account's profile too** — it never touched your account (there is no network call in that path), but it deleted the local mirror including the web-linked profile, which then silently came back with a *new* id on the next sync. It now clears only local profiles and decks, keeps mirrored decks, and says so; the label was misleading too
- **"Create local Profile" was capitalised inconsistently** with every other button
- **Deleting a game left an orphan row in the upload outbox**, pointing at a game log that no longer existed
- **The commander tax chip covered the active-turn timer** — both sat in the bottom-left corner of the player tile, and the chip was drawn on top
- **Poison lagged 1.5 seconds behind your taps** — life already showed its pending change while the batch settled; poison tracked the same pending value internally but never passed it to the screen, so presses looked like they hadn't registered. Poison taps now also give the same haptic feedback life does
- **Commander art beside a deck looked jagged** — the full-size Scryfall art crop was squeezed into a ~40px circle at the lowest filter quality. It now decodes near its display size and resamples properly
- **Opening the card scanner on Linux or Windows hung forever on a loading spinner** — `permission_handler` has no desktop implementation, so the camera-permission request threw and the screen never finished loading, with no way back. Scanning is now correctly reported as unavailable on platforms the `camera` plugin doesn't support, and the entry points say so instead of navigating into a dead screen

### Added
- **Your ManaVortex-Web collection and binders now show up in the Collection screen when signed in** — a read-only mirror, same shape as web decks: pull-to-refresh re-fetches, nothing here can be edited from mobile (that stays on the website), and web-sourced cards are clearly badged and never merged with anything scanned locally, even for the exact same printing
- **Saving a scan session can now also file the cards into a binder** — "Save to Collection" asks which binder (or "Collection only") when at least one binder exists, then clears the scanned list once the save succeeds, since the cards are now filed away and there's nothing left to lose by clearing it

### Fixed
- **My Player Card always said "No deck selected"** — the screen already supported showing and picking a deck, Settings just never passed any decks to it
- **Profiles/Decks left most of the screen empty with few profiles** — the grid was a fixed 5 columns regardless of how many profiles actually exist; it now sizes to the real count (capped at 5), so a single profile's decks are no longer squeezed (and truncated) into a fifth of the width
- **A profile's deck list had no way to tell there was more below the fold** — added a persistent scrollbar; the same account's decks that fit entirely on an iPad's taller tile were silently cut off on iPhone's shorter one
- **Home screen icons stayed a fixed size on tablets**, looking small and lost inside much bigger tiles — they now scale with the tile itself
- **Home and the active game screen ran content under a real device's notch and home indicator** — both set `extendBody`/`extendBodyBehindAppBar` without a `SafeArea`, verified directly against simulated iPhone safe-area insets (content started at the raw screen edge instead of past the 47px/21px real inset). The game screen also needed its tile sizing moved off `MediaQuery.size` and onto the safe-area-aware `LayoutBuilder` constraints, or tiles would overflow the now-smaller safe box
- **The Collection screen's "Scan Cards" button covered the last row of cards** — the list had no bottom padding reserved for the floating button
- **Every card in Collection showed a fake "100%" scan-confidence badge** — hardcoded regardless of the card's real (or nonexistent, for a web-mirrored card) scan quality. Confidence is now scanner/scan-review only, where it's meaningful
- **Tap ripples on the Player Card and match-upload settings rows were silently swallowed** — their rounded background was painted by a plain `Container`, which sits outside any `Material` ancestor, so the `ListTile`s inside had no surface to draw ink splashes on

### Changed
- **Scan Cards is a tile again** — the home screen is a clean 3x2 grid of six equal destinations (Start Game, Profiles/Decks, History, Collection, Scan Cards, Settings) rather than a hero tile plus five, which had no clean way to fit a sixth destination. Scanning still has a shortcut from inside the Collection screen too, for adding more cards without leaving it

### Fixed
- **Scanner preview was stretched horizontally on iOS** — the screen assumed the camera's reported preview size was already portrait-shaped on iOS and only corrected it on Android. It isn't: both platforms report the sensor's native landscape dimensions, so the iOS preview (and the captured card image) was squashed into the wrong aspect ratio. Also locks capture orientation explicitly instead of relying on the live device-rotation stream
- **Opening or closing the scanner briefly flashed the previous screen in the wrong layout** — the orientation switch was requested from `initState`/`dispose`, racing the navigation transition that started immediately after. The switch now happens before the screen is pushed or popped, so the transition doesn't cross a not-yet-rotated frame
- **Logging in was stuck in landscape** — the login form is a narrow portrait layout but inherited the app's landscape-only lock with nothing to relax it. It now switches to portrait on the way in and back to landscape on the way out (back button, system back gesture, and after a successful login), using the same race-free transition as the scanner fix above

### Added
- **Scanning a player card** — when someone shows their card, the setup screen can read it into their seat, so the finished game reaches their account too. Mobile only; the desktop build has no camera
- **A note where player names are typed** — creating a profile now says a nickname is enough, and that names entered for other players are stored with the game and sent to your account if you upload it. It is not worded as consent, because the person typing cannot consent on somebody else's behalf
- **Player card** — signed in, you can show a QR that says "this account was in this seat, playing this deck". Whoever is tracking the game scans it, and the finished match can then reach your history on the website. Fetch it before you sit down: minting needs a connection, though the card stays valid for a week so a table with no signal is fine. Scanning it adds nothing automatically — you confirm the match yourself on the website afterwards and can remove it at any time

### Fixed
- **A duel now seats both players at the short edges, facing each other** — side-by-side tiles each take a quarter turn so they read the right way up from that side. Previously one tile was flipped 180°, which faces the opposite *long* edge and so faced neither player
- **A game with zero turns is no longer reachable** — choosing a starting player is what opens turn 1, and its dialog blocked taps outside but not the system back gesture. Backing out left a game with no turn at all, which could then be ended and published reporting 0 turns

### Changed
- **The game board is black** — it was the theme background, which is near-white in light mode: a glowing rectangle on a dim table, and wasted battery on an OLED screen

### Fixed
- **"Win rate by turn order" on the website was measuring the wrong thing** — the app sent its tile index as `seat`, and the site grouped on it under that heading. They are not the same: the grid is two rows facing each other and turn order walks it clockwise, so tile 3 of 6 is the *sixth* player to act, and the tile index cannot express who started at all. Matches now carry a real `turn_position`, derived from who actually took the first turn
- **Two players now sit across the table from each other** — the board split left/right and rotated the *left* tile 180°, which faces nobody: a player sitting to the side would be reading upside-down text. Two seats are now stacked, far side inverted, exactly as four and six already were
- **Three, five and seven players no longer leave a blank quarter** — the odd row was left-aligned against an empty cell. The short row is centred on the table edge instead
- **The app no longer fails to start where the desktop has no screensaver portal** — `WakelockPlus.enable()` throws `DBusServiceUnknownException` when `org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop` is missing, and it threw out of `main()` before the first frame. A missing screen-dim inhibitor is now logged and ignored
- **The in-game menu painted over its own buttons** — its seven rows were `ListTile`s inside a colour-filled `Container`, which hides the tile background and ink splash and trips a framework assertion in debug builds. The same defect was fixed for deck and profile rows in 0.9.0; the menu was missed because nothing had ever opened it in a test

### Fixed
- **You can now actually cast your commander** — the event existed, was translated into four languages, and rendered in the game log, but nothing in the app ever raised it: `castCommander` lived only on `GameSession` with no button attached. So the commander tax added in 0.9.4 could never appear, and every published match reported zero commander casts. The tile's tax chip is now the control: tap it to cast, long-press to send the commander back to the command zone

### Added
- **Commander tax on the player tile** — after your first cast, each tile shows what the next one costs from the command zone (`+2` per previous cast, CR 903.8). The count was already tracked and even uploaded; nothing displayed it, which is the moment it is actually useful
- **Paused time in post-game stats** — shown only when the timer was actually paused, so a slow turn and an interrupted one stop reading the same

### Fixed
- **Partner commanders were dropped at game start** — every deck source captures the second commander, but nothing carried it into the game: the engine's `partnerName` was never populated, so the log, the projection and the published match kept only the primary. Partner decks now keep both, and the website can be told which pair was played
- **Turn time is now folded by the engine** — `computeStats` recorded turn durations into the log and never read them back, while the read-side adapter kept its own parallel tally. The engine is the single source of truth again, which also means the upload path can carry it

### Changed
- **Deck names on the website's Matches page link to the deck** — only where the seat played a deck from your own account; a hand-typed deck name has nothing to link to and stays plain text

### Fixed
- **A failed account action now says why** — refreshing web decks, flushing the upload queue and deleting cloud history each reported failure as a bare `null`/`false`/"skipped", which reads exactly like "there was nothing to do". That is how a broken delete went unnoticed: the button returned a quiet no while the server kept every match. The reason is retained on `AuthState.lastRemoteError` and logged

### Fixed
- **Game log timeline was English-only** — the live game log, the thing players read *during* a game, had no localization at all. Every event line ("dealt 5 damage to …", "was eliminated"), every elimination reason, every event-type filter name and the whole filter row are now translated
- **Game statistics screen was English-only** — the entire screen was hardcoded English despite the app shipping in four languages, so a German, French or Spanish player finished a game and hit an untranslated wall. All 47 strings are now localized
- **Highlight categories could not be translated** — the deck-stats highlight counts were keyed by their English display text (`'Executioner'`, `'Focused Fire'`), so translating the labels would have silently broken the lookup and left the counts empty. Categories now use stable ids with the label resolved at render time
- **"Life Lost" in post-game stats was wrong** — it counted only direct life changes, so a player who went from 40 to 19 on commander damage read "Life Lost: 0". It now shows every point of life lost however it was tracked, with an "as damage / paid–drained" breakdown underneath when the game was detailed enough to know
- **Deck list no longer shows the first deck twice** — with no deck picked yet, the top "selected" row and the list below both rendered the first deck, because the list filtered against the not-yet-set selection instead of the row actually pinned
- **Guest option no longer disappears after picking a deck** — the profile list was refreshed from storage without re-appending the ephemeral Guest entry, dropping it from every tile until the setup screen was reopened
- **Deck and profile rows paint their selection correctly** — both were `ListTile`s inside a colour-filled `Container`, which hides the tile's own background and ink splash (and trips a framework assertion in debug builds); they now use a `Material` instead
- **Scanner: fewer false negatives** — frames required before auto-capture drop from 3 → 2 for a set-only match and 6 → 3 for name-only; audio feedback is wrapped so a sound failure can no longer surface as a scan error
- **Login survives being offline** — app startup no longer signs the user out when the backend is unreachable. Only a genuine authentication failure (401/403 or a dead refresh token) clears the stored session; a transport error keeps it, which matters for a local-first app opened at a kitchen table with no signal

### Removed
- **Backup & Restore** — the local JSON export/import feature was removed (`BackupService`, `BackupScreen`, and the Settings entry). Cloud sync via a ManaVortex-Web account is the planned replacement; see `PLAN_gamelog_redesign.md`.
- **Legacy game-log layer** — the in-memory `CommanderGame` + `GameLogService` + `GameController` layer and the `game_log_*` SQLite tables were removed, replaced by the event-sourcing engine (see Changed).
- **LAN Network Sharing** — mDNS device discovery and the local HTTP sync server were removed (`nsd`/`shelf`/`shelf_router`/`network_info_plus` deps dropped). Cross-device sync moves to the cloud op-log path.
- **Demo Data loader** — the Settings "Load Demo Data" convenience and its service were removed.

### Added
- **Upload status in Settings** — with match upload switched on, Settings → Account now shows whether anything is still waiting to be sent, why the last attempt failed, and a "Retry now" action. Without it the outbox was invisible: uploads could fail silently game after game with nothing on screen to say so
- **Match history upload (opt-in)** — finished games can be published to your ManaVortex-Web account so they appear on the website. Off by default and separate from logging in: signing in brings your decks down, uploading your games is its own choice, since the record includes the player names you typed for everyone at the table. Games queue locally when there is no connection and are sent on the next login or app resume; a game corrected after the fact is re-sent and overwrites its earlier copy. Settings → Account also offers "Delete cloud match history", which purges the server copy and leaves local games untouched
- **Name-only decks for any player** — every seat, including Guests, can now type a deck name in the deck panel (reached by tapping the already-selected profile). Guest decks are ephemeral and live only in that game; on a stored profile the deck is saved for reuse. Sibling Guest seats still cannot share a deck name, which is what keeps them apart in the game log. These carry no card list, printings or prices — those come from the website
- **Web decks in player slots** — logging in with a ManaVortex-Web account now pulls that account's decks into the app and offers them when picking a deck for a player. Decks are cached locally, so they stay available offline, and a "Refresh decks" action in Settings → Account re-pulls them on demand. The account is bound to one local profile (an existing profile of the same name is adopted rather than duplicated). Decks stay read-only here — they are built and edited on the website; see `PLAN_web_integration.md`
- **Event-sourcing engine** — new pure-Dart packages `packages/mtg_engine` (typed events, single reducer, stats, hybrid-logical-clock ordering, conflict-free merge) and `packages/mtg_store` (transactional SQLite op log, projection cache, sync plumbing). Now the app's game-log layer (see Changed); groundwork for future multi-device cloud sync.
- **Account Login (optional)** — sign in with a ManaVortex-Web account from Settings → Account. Additive and offline-first: the app remains fully usable without logging in. Access/refresh tokens are stored in the platform secure store (Keychain/Keystore), the access token auto-refreshes, and the mobile session uses a ~90-day sliding refresh window so an active user effectively never re-logs in. Account creation opens the web app in the browser

### Changed
- **Life loss is accounted in two parts** — `PlayerStats.lifeLost` became `lifeLostOther` (life paid or drained) alongside the existing `damageReceived`, with `lifeLostTotal` summing them. The distinction is real in Magic — damage causes life loss but is not life loss, and only damage can be prevented or trigger lifelink — but it depends on whether a player attributes damage or just taps the life counter. So the total is always correct, and the breakdown appears only when the log genuinely knows it
- **Deck name and commander are recorded separately** — `PlayerRef`/`PlayerState` gained `deckName` and `deckWebId` alongside `commanderName`, so a game log distinguishes "Atraxa Superfriends" (the deck), "Atraxa, Praetors' Voice" (the commander) and the web deck's id. Older logs, which stored the deck name in `commanderName`, keep reading correctly through the new `effectiveDeckName`/`effectiveCommanderName` getters
- **Game log runs on the event-sourcing engine** — the live game, undo/redo, resume, stats, history, and the log timeline are now projections of an HLC-ordered op log (`mtg_engine` + `mtg_store`), replacing the in-memory `CommanderGame` + `GameLogService` dual-state layer. The active game resumes by replaying its op log (no `savedGameState` snapshot). Profile/deck writes are now transactional, retiring the old load-all/save-all race.
